# Webflow API

> Reverse-engineered internal API. Unofficial — may change without notice.

## Authentication
Cookie-based (wfsession) — Authentication method detected from captured traffic.

### Providing credentials
- Prefer passing auth as request headers or cookies at call time (do not hardcode secrets into the skill).
- If executing via an external proxy/executor, pass per-call credentials (cookies and/or headers) so they are not persisted.

## Dependencies
- Runtime capable of HTTPS requests.
- If using `scripts/api.ts`: TypeScript toolchain (or transpile to JS).

## Endpoints

### Auth Flow (1)
- `GET /api/user/authenticated` — Check if a user is currently authenticated.

### Data Read (1)
- `GET /cm/{cmId}/translations/en.json` — Retrieve English translations for a content module.

### Data Write (4)
- `POST /clientlogger` — Log client-side events and errors to Webflow.
- `POST /context-v2/{context-v2Id}` — Update a specific context within Webflow's system.
- `POST /prediction/{predictionId}` — Submit a prediction result to Webflow.
- `POST /r/t/csp/reportOnly` — Report CSP violations in report-only mode to Webflow.

Here are some quick examples to get you started interacting with the Webflow API:

// This is a common read operation for accessing localized content.

console.log(translations);
```

console.log(logResult);
```

## About This Skill

This skill provides access to Webflow's internal API — the hidden endpoints that power their web/mobile app.
These are NOT official public APIs. They were captured by observing network traffic while using the site.

**Important:**
- Auth tokens in `auth.json` may expire — re-capture if you get 401 errors
- Internal APIs can change without notice — endpoints may break
- Rate limits are unknown — be conservative with request frequency

## When to Use This Skill

Use this skill when you need to:
- Access Webflow data without official API access
- Automate actions on webflow.com (faster than browser automation)
- Call the same endpoints the Webflow frontend uses

## Error Handling

```typescript
try {
  const data = await client.get("/resource");
} catch (err) {
  if (err.message.includes("401")) {
    // Auth expired — need to re-capture
    console.error("Auth expired, re-run unbrowse_login");
  } else {
    console.error("API error:", err.message);
  }
}
```
